checks.what: vichy-france gain from french-third-republic, July 1940 (the German-occupied zone). republic-of-china gain from manchukuo, August 1945 (Manchuria without Dalian, Hulunbuir, the Xing'an lands). Page: 'At one minute past midnight Trans-Baikal time on 9 August 1945'; the Soviets 'toppled the Japanese puppet states of Manchukuo in Manchuria and Mengjiang in Inner Mongolia'. The page does not name the ROC as the heir: that is the manchukuo dossier's successor, applied in August instead of at year end, as ROC/ledger/66 does for Rehe. A gain moves only the cells Manchukuo holds, so the place circles cannot spill. Trial: Manchuria 4,036 cells ROC land under Soviet occupation at the end of 1945 (draft: 3,995 ROC direct, no occupation shown); 1946 unchanged (ROC, contested).

Soviet occupation_start of republic-of-china, September 1945, region Manchuria (4,060 cells). Page infobox: 'Soviet occupation of Inner Mongolia and Manchuria until 1946'; campaign '8 August - 2 September 1945'. It repeats Soviet ledger/46 in month 9 so it runs after events/6; the occupation was in force in September. Closed by Soviet ledger/55 (1946).

Soviet occupation_start of republic-of-china, September 1945, region the whole Inner Mongol admin-1. The page supports a Soviet occupation of Inner Mongolia until 1946 but gives no extent. With the whole province, the 1,878 former Mengjiang cells became Soviet-occupied ROC land; Soviet ledger/55's 1946 occupation_end then counts as an event of 1946 on them, so the communist-party-of-china_1946 keyframe (a dossier verdict: the Liberated Zone as Cliopatria's 1947 outline) could no longer take them: trial snap 'added 2586' fell to 'added 781, kept by others 1836', and 1,805 cells of central Inner Mongolia that are CPC in the draft became ROC in 1946 (with keyframe_overrides/1) or grey (without it). Fixed by narrowing the region to Inner Mongolia minus Cliopatria's CPC 1947 outline. Trial after fix: end of 1945, 2,916 cells Soviet-occupied ROC land (Xing'an, Hulunbuir and the west; draft 1,158), central Inner Mongolia 1,806 nobody as in the draft; 1946: CPC 1,824 as in the draft, ROC 3,630, nobody 31 (draft 2,463); 1947 on identical to the draft.
checks.fix: Region now {minus: [Inner Mongol, Cliopatria Communist Party of China 1947]}; note extended with the reason.

union-of-soviet-socialist-republics_1943: the dossier's correction (kept verbatim as the first union member) plus 19 admin-1s retaken in 1943. Pages: Battle of the Dnieper (26 August - 23 December 1943: 'Soviets reclaim left-bank Ukraine, including the city of Kiev and Donets basin'; 'The west bank was still in German hands for the most part'); Eastern Front ('Orel (retaken by the Red Army on 5 August 1943)', 'Kharkov was abandoned for the final time on 22 August'); Battle of Kursk ('Kursk was retaken by the Soviets on 8 February 1943, and Rostov on 14 February'); Smolensk Operation (Smolensk liberated 25 September; the goal 'to clear the German presence from the Smolensk and Bryansk regions'). Kaluga, Tula, the west of Moscow Oblast and Lipetsk were behind the front all year. The agent called Rostov 'pages silent', but the Kursk page it opened dates it; 63 Rostov cells (Rostov to the Mius) were nobody at the end of 1943, so Rostov was added. Approximation left in place: the whole Kiev and Dnipropetrovs'k oblasts include right-bank land (about 34 cells south of the Kiev bridgehead, about 41 around Kryvyi Rih and Nikopol) still German at the end of 1943; the pages opened do not place the year-end front there, so it is not cut. Trial after fix: snap added 742 and removed 591 (draft: added 14, removed 1,800); Rostov 404 of 405 cells Soviet.
checks.fix: Added {admin1: Rostov, country: Russia} to the retaken-land union (source: Battle of Kursk page, 'Rostov on 14 February' 1943); why extended.

problems: Cross-window (p1950-p1959): events/4 and keyframe_overrides/6 keep Italian Somaliland british-africa land until the british-africa_1953 snap, but the Italian Somaliland page has 'End of British occupation: 1 April 1950' and 'came under British military administration until 1950, when it became a United Nations trusteeship'. british-africa/ledger/51 (April 1950 occupation_end) closes nothing, because the relation closed when italian-africa ended in 1943. p1950-p1959 should add {slug: british-africa, year: 1950, month: 4, type: loss, counterpart: nobody (or a trust-territory dossier if one is added), region: {country: Somalia}, source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Somaliland}.

Dossier union-of-soviet-socialist-republics ledger/47 and ledger/56 (repeated by patch events/8) mark the Soviet occupation over the whole Inner Mongol admin-1, which includes about 1,158 ROC-held cells of western Inner Mongolia (Alxa, Ordos, west of 108E) that were never Mengjiang or Manchukuo. The page names only 'Mengjiang in Inner Mongolia', and the hatch over them is already in the draft. Dossier fix: narrow ledger/47 and ledger/56 to the Mengjiang and Xing'an lands.

Compiler behaviour worth knowing: an occupation_end in a year counts as an event on its cells, so no keyframe can take them that year. This is why the Inner Mongolia override was needed and why a Soviet occupation drawn over CPC-claimed land blocked communist-party-of-china_1946. Other windows that re-time occupations should check the following year's keyframes.

Residual: Cliopatria's 1941 Vichy free zone is wider than the armistice line in Burgundy and the Centre (Côte-d'Or, Nièvre, Saône-et-Loire, Allier, Cher, Indre-et-Loire, Loir-et-Cher), so those occupied cells stay unhatched Vichy land 1940-42, as in the draft.

Residual, approximate: keyframe_overrides/0 draws all of Kiev and Dnipropetrovs'k oblasts Soviet at the end of 1943, including about 75 right-bank cells (south of the Kiev bridgehead, Kryvyi Rih and Nikopol) that were still German. The pages opened do not place that front. Krasnodar (105 cells) and Crimea (82) stay nobody at the end of 1943; Crimea should be German-held ('the Crimea was now cut off', Battle of the Dnieper page), not nobody's.

Window report inaccuracies: Rostov was not 'pages silent' (Battle of Kursk page: 'Rostov on 14 February' 1943; added to keyframe_overrides/0). The British Africa overrides do create a conflict after all: 3 Libyan border cells against Egypt's keyframes, rightly won by British Africa.
